articles.title: Isaac Heeney ‘looking forward’ to addressing Sydney teammates as banned players return to club
articles.summary: Heeney, Warner, Blakey, Jordon and Bice attend exit meetings. The five have not been to Swans HQ since August suspension. Sydney vice-captain Isaac Heeney says he is looking forward to addressing his teammates after the Swans’ five suspended players made their return to the club’s headquarters.
body: Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice on Wednesday appeared at the Swans’ base at Moore Park for the first time since being banned for breaching club standards in August.
Warner and Bice first arrived together, followed by Heeney, Blakey and Jordon in the same car.
Warner, flanked by a silent Bice, said he was “just here for my exit interview”.
Asked if he was going to say sorry or anything at all, Warner said: “I don’t know.”

articles.title: 'Start-up' Newcastle tapping into Red Bulls spirit
articles.summary: Head coach Dan McFarland is excited to have the backing of Newcastle Red Bulls' owners as he tries to fuse a new team together in the Prem this season.
body: It is all change at Newcastle Red Bulls as they prepare for the new Prem season, but they plan to tackle it with the sort of fearless approach for which their owners are renowned.
With Red Bull taking over at Kingston Park in August 2025, it was a scramble to get things in place for last season.
As a result, Newcastle could not bridge the gap to the other nine teams and finished bottom for a fourth successive campaign, with just two wins in 18 games.

But, after a huge influx of players in the summer, 'Red Bulls 2.0' under new head coach Dan McFarland are ready to embrace the challenge as they begin with a daunting trip to champions Northampton Saints on Friday night.

articles.title: Brisbane to appeal Lachie Neale’s ban in desperate bid to play AFL grand final
articles.summary: Dual Brownlow medallist guilty of intentional striking. Plea of ‘exceptional circumstances’ rejected by tribunal. Brisbane will head to the AFL appeals board in a desperate bid to free suspended star Lachie Neale for the grand final.
body: Neale remains banned for the premiership decider against Fremantle after failing to argue his way out of a one-match suspension for a gut punch on Hawthorn’s Jack Ginnivan.

To succeed at an appeals board hearing, expected on Thursday, Brisbane will have to prove the tribunal finding was either an error of law, an unreasonable decision, a manifestly excessive classification, or a manifestly excessive sanction.

“There’s been 10 [gut punch] incidents this year, all of them have resulted in a week [suspension],” the AFL’s footy boss Greg Swann said on Wednesday. “That was the third [tribunal] appeal and they’ve all been upheld.”
At the end of a four-and-a-half hour hearing on Tuesday night, the tribunal decided not to enact the “exceptional and compelling clause” to allow Neale to avoid suspension.

articles.title: Contagious, confident - the rise of Lewis Koumas
articles.summary: Having made his mark in the early stages of the season at Liverpool, Lewis Koumas will aim to continue his good form with Wales in the Nations League.
body: It took less than a week of pre-season for the 21-year-old to show new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola what he could offer.
And it has taken less than a month of the new season for him to show why he has a place in Liverpool's plans.

Now, over the next fortnight, the attacking prospect who is fast becoming an Anfield favourite will attempt to prove what several people in Welsh football have suspected for a long while - that he can have a big impact on the international stage too.

"I feel he's going to be a really important player for us for a number of years," Wales boss Craig Bellamy said before Nations League games with Portugal, Denmark and Norway that will see Koumas share an international stage with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo and Erling Haaland.

articles.title: MLS coach sacked after sexist remark to female referee
articles.summary: MLS club Columbus Crew sack their reserve team coach after he refused to let go of a female referee's hand and says "don't forget this is a man's game".
body: Major League Soccer club Columbus Crew have sacked their reserve team coach after he refused to let go of a female referee's hand and said "don't forget this is a man's game".
Federico Higuain, brother of former Real Madrid striker Gonzalo Higuain, was sent off and given a two-match suspension for the incident during an MLS Next Pro league match.
"We determined it's in the best interest of our club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higuain from his responsibilities," Crew general manager Issa Tall said in a statement.
"After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met."

articles.title: From leaving Rangers to La Liga - Scotland is next step for Ure
articles.summary: Robbie Ure has made it all the way to Sevilla since failing to break through at Rangers and now a first Scotland cap awaits the striker, writes Tom English.
body: Robbie Ure, cool and confident and 22 years old, played 90 minutes for Sevilla against Barcelona at the weekend; 90 minutes of being marked by Pau Cubarsi, man of the match in the World Cup final, 90 minutes of pitch-time with Rodri, player of the tournament, 90 minutes of breathing the same rarefied air as Lamine Yamal.
Ure is a part of a new-ish wave of Scotland striker, uncapped but hopeful of making a debut on Saturday away to Slovenia in the Nations League.

There is no Lyndon Dykes in Sebastien Pocognoli's squad and no George Hirst. Injury has ruled out Che Adams, Lawrence Shankland and Ross Stewart. Those five were all at the World Cup in the United States during the summer.
Now, it's Ure alongside James Wilson of Hearts and Kieron Bowie of Sassuolo, who both have two caps, and Oli McBurnie of Hull, with the last of his 16 international appearances coming five years ago.

articles.title: Caldentey’s late penalty provides WCL relief for struggling Arsenal against Køge
articles.summary: Mariona Caldentey’s 93rd-minute penalty delivered a win and a hefty dose of relief to fans bouncing behind the goal in the North Bank after the ball hit the back of the net, but ­Arsenal’s narrow defeat of HB Køge in their Champions League opener left more questions unanswered than answered for the…
body: The puffed cheeks of the manager, Renée Slegers, said it all when the full-time whistle went. If it had been revealed after the final whistle that a force field surrounded the opposition goal at Meadow Park, many would have believed it, such was the extent of Arsenal’s ridiculous profligacy in front of goal in their league-phase opener.
“It was a mentality and resilience win today,” said Slegers. “The football didn’t give us the win … but we get the goal as a squad.”
Exactly what is stopping Arsenal from getting the ball in the back of the net with a swagger reflective of their talent-laden squad is hard to pinpoint.

Yes, teams are defending excellently against them, as a battling Køge and their goalkeeper Alberte Vingum did on Tuesday night, but this feels like an Arsenal problem: a mentality one, a training ground one, a ruthlessness one.

articles.title: Gonzalo Higuain’s brother sacked by MLS club after telling female referee ‘this is a man’s game’
articles.summary: MLS club Columbus Crew have sacked their reserve team manager Federico Higuain after he was alleged to have refused to let go of the hand of a female referee and told her “don’t forget that this is a man’s game”.
body: Higuain, the brother of former Argentina international striker Gonzalo Higuain, was sent off and suspended for two matches following the incident, which occurred during a 1-0 defeat to Huntsville City in the MLS NEXT Pro series on 23 August.

The MLS referees union, The Professional Soccer Referees Association (PSRA), criticised the league’s response and said it fell “drastically short” in a statement Sunday 20 September, after Higuain had returned to the touchline for two Crew 2 matches.

Without naming Higuain, the PSRA said a “male head coach committed two deliberate acts of physical abuse and sexism against a female official - squeezing her hand and refusing to let go after being told to stop three times.”
The PSRA also said “this physical intimidation was compounded by a demeaning, sexist remark to the official: 'Don't forget, this is a man's game’.”

articles.title: The Italian Job gets a sequel! Can Mancini inspire a new generation?
articles.summary: This year, Italian football fell to its lowest ebb. In Europe, no Italian club made it past the quarter-finals - while Atalanta were the only Serie A side to reach the Champions League last 16. But that was nothing compared to the national team.
body: Roberto Mancini is back as Italy head coach after a second spell; the former Man City boss won Euro 2020 with the Azzurri, who have not qualified for the last three World Cups; With exclusive insight from Gianluigi Donnarumma, Sky Sports' Sam Blitz analyses the road back for Italy...
Italy did not qualify for the third World Cup in a row. An unthinkable prospect given they have won the competition four times.
The first two failures to qualify were masked over by the Euro 2020 triumph at Wembley. That at least gave the nation hope.

The third World Cup failure was one last straw. A 48-team World Cup did not include Italy. It brought about the resignations of not just head coach Gennaro Gattuso, but also Italian FA president Gabriele Gravina and Gianluigi Buffon as the team's head of delegation.

articles.title: Can Europe inspire new 'Medinah miracle' at Presidents Cup?
articles.summary: If the International Team are going to end Team USA’s Presidents Cup dominance this week, live on Sky Sports, they may require their own 'Miracle at Medinah' to do it.
body: Fourteen years on from Team Europe producing a historic final-day comeback to claim Ryder Cup glory at the same venue, Geoff Ogilvy sees his side head in as heavy underdogs to avoid an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup defeat.

The United States have won every edition since 2005 and only been beaten once in the event's history, before seven of the 24 players involved in this year's contest were even born, with all logic pointing to that run continuing in Illinois.

Nothing less than victory will be acceptable for Team USA, 12 months on from a humbling home Ryder Cup loss where only a singles fightback prevented a heavier defeat, with Brandt Snedeker aware of the expectation to deliver.
"It's the elephant in the room you have to address," Snedeker said. "Just because these last (Presidents Cup) teams have been successful, doesn't mean we're going to be successful.

articles.title: Tampa Bay Rays Secure AL East Crown: 'It's A Tough Division'
articles.summary: Playing in perhaps baseball’s toughest division, the Tampa Bay Rays were the class of the field this season
body: The thrifty Rays clinched their fifth AL East title with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees in the second game of a day-night doubleheader Tuesday as Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 innings and Yandy Diaz hit a pair of two-run singles.

Tampa Bay took the AL East for the first time since 2021 and surpassed that team by three days with the earliest division clincher in team history. The club also won division crowns in the pandemic-shortened 2020 season along with 2010 and 2008, when it reached the World Series and had the franchise's first winning season.

"It means a lot," Díaz said through a translator. "It’s a tough division. It’s a competitive division almost every single year. With this group we knew that from the beginning, but we still believed in ourselves every single way. So here we are in Yankee Stadium celebrating and we feel really happy that we got the job done."
